paper_metadata.title: Clock Quantum Monte Carlo: an imaginary-time method for real-time quantum dynamics

summary: The paper presents a classical FCIQMC-based simulation of gate-model quantum dynamics using the Feynman-Kitaev Clock Hamiltonian. It reports numerical examples on 11 qubits with 128 time points, achieving over 95% parallel efficiency on 2 processors and about 70% on 8 processors, with an inferred ~14x speedup in the strong-scaling plot; no quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Clock Quantum Monte Carlo applied to quantum circuit dynamics via the Feynman-Kitaev Clock Hamiltonian, with numerical examples on local rotations and circuits containing CNOT gates, including basis-rotation mitigation and parallel-in-time scaling.

algorithm.variant: FCIQMC applied to the Feynman-Kitaev Clock Hamiltonian for real-time quantum dynamics
algorithm.convergence_criteria: simulation run until walker population equilibrates and time-averaged observables converge
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state fixed by penalty term C0 to the known initial state |Ψ0⟩; walkers initialized for the chosen circuit/time history state

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum circuit dynamics are mapped to a ground-state problem using the Feynman-Kitaev Clock Hamiltonian on a system-time Hilbert space
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize the Clock Hamiltonian H = H' + C0 whose ground state is the history state encoding the full unitary evolution
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty operator C0 fixes the initial state at t=0; no QUBO/Ising encoding
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = H' + C0, where H' is the time-embedded Hamiltonian and C0 = (I - |Ψ0⟩⟨Ψ0|) ⊗ |0⟩⟨0|

problem_instance.description: Toy quantum dynamics examples: single-qubit local rotations applied uniformly to 11 qubits, and circuits with local rotations plus variable numbers of CNOT gates; also a parallel scaling study on a 11-qubit, 128-time-point circuit

dataset_specification.description: Quantum circuit instances defined in the paper; no external dataset

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No data preprocessing; circuit states and basis rotations are defined analytically
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Expectation value of Sz at final time versus mean walker number; comparison across rotation angles and with/without basis rotations; strong-scaling benchmark over processor counts

noise_model.mitigation_details: Basis rotations used to mitigate the sign problem; no hardware noise mitigation
noise_model.classical_solver: FCIQMC / interacting walker Monte Carlo on CPU cluster
noise_model.classical_postprocessing: Time-averaged observables and autocorrelation correction; annihilation of walkers; strong-scaling speedup/efficiency analysis

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: transition from sign-incoherent to sign-coherent sampling as walker number increases

speedup_claims.conditions: strong scaling on a 11-qubit, 128-time-point circuit with a simple MPI implementation
speedup_claims.caveats: Efficiency is reported for 2 processors; no exact wall-clock times are provided.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly given; discussion notes generic sign-problem difficulty and parallel-in-time scaling

limiting_factors: No quantum-vs-classical performance comparison on a QPU

notes: This paper is not a gate-based quantum computing experiment; it is a classical simulation method for quantum circuit dynamics using FCIQMC and the Feynman-Kitaev Clock.
